sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》旗下的每日新闻简报《DealBook》报道商业与政策新闻。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的 DealBook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的现场对话。

sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日通过 NYTimes.com 进行部分采访的直播，供所有人免费观看。

If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today, early in his presidency, Donald Trump called for a federal commission to investigate an issue that was personal for him.
sentences.zh: 今天，唐纳德·特朗普在总统任期初期，呼吁成立一个联邦委员会，调查一个对他个人而言至关重要的问题。

sentences.en: Voter fraud in the 2016 election.
sentences.zh: 2016年大选中的选民欺诈问题。

sentences.en: Now, that commission is requesting data on 200 million American voters, and the states are fighting back.
sentences.zh: 现在，该委员会正在要求获取2亿美国选民的数据，而各州正在进行反击。

sentences.en: It's Monday, July 17th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月17日，星期一。

sentences.en: Michael Lyons, why does Donald Trump say he lost the popular vote?
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·莱昂斯，为什么唐纳德·特朗普说他输掉了普选票？

sentences.en: He believes it was stolen.
sentences.zh: 他认为选举被窃取了。

sentences.en: The winner, who came in second, tweeted, in addition to winning the Electoral College in a landslide, I won the popular vote if you deduct
sentences.zh: 这位最终排名第二的获胜者发推文称：除了以压倒性优势赢得选举人团投票外，如果扣除

sentences.en: the millions of people who voted illegally.
sentences.zh: 数百万非法投票的人，我也赢得了普选票。

sentences.en: He says that there were at least 3 million, possibly more, illegal voters.
sentences.zh: 他说至少有300万人，甚至可能更多，是非法选民。

sentences.en: Serious voter fraud in Virginia, New Hampshire, and California.
sentences.zh: 弗吉尼亚州、新罕布什尔州和加利福尼亚州存在严重的选民欺诈。

sentences.en: So why isn't the media reporting on this?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么媒体不报道这件事呢？

sentences.en: Serious bias, big problem.
sentences.zh: 严重的偏见，大问题。

sentences.en: You look at the dead people that are registered to vote, who vote.
sentences.zh: 看看那些已登记投票但已经去世的人，他们也投了票。

sentences.en: You look at people that are registered in two states.
sentences.zh: 看看那些在两个州重复登记的人。

sentences.en: He alludes that many of them probably were undocumented immigrants.
sentences.zh: 他暗示其中许多人可能是无证移民。

sentences.en: Of those votes cast, none of them come to me.
sentences.zh: 在这些投出的选票中，没有一张是投给我的。

sentences.en: None of them come to me.
sentences.zh: 没有一张是投给我的。

sentences.en: They would all be for the other side.
sentences.zh: 它们全都是投给对方的。

sentences.en: None of them come to me.
sentences.zh: 没有一张是投给我的。

sentences.en: And he thinks that they all voted for Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 而他认为这些人全都投给了希拉里·克林顿。

sentences.en: Millions of people agree with me when I say that.
sentences.zh: 当我这么说时，有数百万人同意我的观点。

sentences.en: And is there any evidence of that?
sentences.zh: 那有什么证据吗？

sentences.en: No, there's not a shred of evidence.
sentences.zh: 没有，一点证据都没有。

sentences.en: And how do you know that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么知道的？

sentences.en: Well, firstly, because I think most experts would say it would be virtually impossible to conceal 3 million illegal votes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，我认为大多数专家会说，隐瞒300万张非法选票几乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: But I called up 49 of the 50 states, dealt with election officials in each of the states asking how much fraud they had found.
sentences.zh: 但我给50个州中的49个打了电话，与每个州的选举官员沟通，询问他们发现了多少欺诈行为。

sentences.en: And by and large, they either found no fraud whatsoever, or very, very small numbers of accusations of fraud.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，他们要么根本没有发现任何欺诈，要么只有极少数关于欺诈的指控。

sentences.en: How long does it take to call 49 states?
sentences.zh: 给49个州打电话需要多长时间？

sentences.en: It took me about five days.
sentences.zh: 我花了大约五天时间。

sentences.en: And one of them, New Jersey, I could never get through to the state official.
sentences.zh: 其中一个州，新泽西州，我一直没能联系上州政府官员。

sentences.en: So I wound up calling every county in New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 所以我最后给新泽西州的每个县都打了电话。

sentences.en: So that was the 15th state?
sentences.zh: 所以那是第15个州？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But no election fraud in that state of New Jersey either?
sentences.zh: 但新泽西州也没有选举欺诈？

sentences.en: Out of all the counties I called, there wasn't a single case.
sentences.zh: 在我打过电话的所有县里，没有发现一个案例。

sentences.en: So what happens, despite everything you've just told me, once Donald Trump becomes president?
sentences.zh: 那么，尽管你刚才告诉了我这一切，唐纳德·特朗普当选总统后会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, he gets into office and he was concerned from the very start about the legitimacy of his victory.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他上任后，从一开始就担心自己胜利的合法性。

sentences.en: He kept complaining that he hadn't won the popular vote.
sentences.zh: 他不断抱怨自己没有赢得普选票。

sentences.en: And so eventually he said,
sentences.zh: 所以最终他说，

sentences.en: I'm going to set up a commission to look into voter fraud, election integrity, and to make sure that everything's straight.
sentences.zh: 我要成立一个委员会来调查选民欺诈、选举公正性，并确保一切都清清楚楚。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So who leads this commission?
sentences.zh: 那么谁来领导这个委员会？

sentences.en: Well, officially it's headed by Vice President Pence.
sentences.zh: 嗯，官方是由彭斯副总统领导的。

sentences.en: The de facto head is a fellow named Chris
sentences.zh: 但事实上的负责人是一个叫克里斯·

sentences.en: Kobach, who is the Secretary of State of Kansas.
sentences.zh: 科巴赫的人，他是堪萨斯州的州务卿。

sentences.en: What do we need to know about Chris Kobach?
sentences.zh: 关于克里斯·科巴赫，我们需要了解什么？

sentences.en: Who exactly is he?
sentences.zh: 他到底是谁？

sentences.en: Mr. Kobach is a dyed-in-the-wool Republican.
sentences.zh: 科巴赫先生是一位彻头彻尾的共和党人。

sentences.en: He has established himself, I think, as probably the leading advocate of strict laws governing who can and cannot be allowed to register to vote or to cast ballots.
sentences.zh: 我认为他已经确立了自己作为严格限制选民登记和投票资格法律的主要倡导者的地位。

sentences.en: He's a very strong proponent of the idea that voter fraud in this country is rampant.
sentences.zh: 他非常强烈地主张这个国家的选民欺诈现象猖獗。

sentences.en: And in fact, like the president, he has said that it's entirely plausible that Donald Trump's victory in the popular vote was stolen from him.
sentences.zh: 事实上，就像总统一样，他说唐纳德·特朗普的普选票胜利被窃取是完全可能的。

sentences.en: And as best we can tell, you've been looking at this subject and at Chris Kobach for many months.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，你已经研究这个课题和克里斯·科巴赫好几个月了。

sentences.en: Where do his views on voter fraud come from?
sentences.zh: 他对选民欺诈的看法从何而来？

sentences.en: Probably a couple of places.
sentences.zh: 可能来自几个方面。

sentences.en: I think that they are rooted in his dedication to another idea, which is that immigration in this country has been counterproductive.
sentences.zh: 我认为它们植根于他对比另一个理念的执着，即这个国家的移民政策适得其反。

sentences.en: KCMO Talk Radio 710.
sentences.zh: KCMO 谈话电台 710。

sentences.en: Has he said that?
sentences.zh: 他这么说过吗？

sentences.en: Has he articulated that?
sentences.zh: 他表达过这种观点吗？

sentences.en: He has.
sentences.zh: 他表达过。

sentences.en: He's the ACLU's worst nightmare because he knows the Constitution and fights to keep them from making confetti of it.
sentences.zh: 他是美国公民自由联盟（ACLU）最可怕的噩梦，因为他了解宪法，并努力阻止他们将其撕成碎片。

sentences.en: He's Chris Kobach.
sentences.zh: 他是克里斯·科巴赫。

sentences.en: And this is The Chris Kobach Show.
sentences.zh: 这是《克里斯·科巴赫秀》。

sentences.en: On a radio show that he hosted.
sentences.zh: 在他主持的一个广播节目中。

sentences.en: You know, what protects us in America from any kind of ethnic cleansing is the rule of law, of course.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在美国，保护我们免受任何形式种族清洗的是法治，当然。

sentences.en: And the rule of law used to be unassailable, used to be taken for granted in America.
sentences.zh: 法治曾经是不可动摇的，在美国曾经被认为是理所当然的。

sentences.en: And now, of course, we have a president who disregards the law when it suits his interests.
sentences.zh: 而现在，当然，我们有一位在符合自己利益时无视法律的总统。

sentences.en: And so, you know, while I normally would answer that by saying, Steve, you know, of course we have the rule that could never happen in America.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，虽然我通常会回答说，史蒂夫，你知道，当然我们有法治，这在美国永远不会发生。

sentences.en: I wonder what can happen.
sentences.zh: 我不知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: I still don't think it's going to happen in America, but I have to admit that things are things are strange and they're happening.
sentences.zh: 我仍然认为这不会在美国发生，但我必须承认事情很奇怪，而且正在发生。

sentences.en: Mr. Kobach was always a conservative and a very well-educated man.
sentences.zh: 科巴赫先生一直是一位保守派，也是一位受过良好教育的人。

sentences.en: He went to Harvard.
sentences.zh: 他去了哈佛大学。

sentences.en: He then went to Oxford.
sentences.zh: 然后去了牛津大学。

sentences.en: He went to Yale Law School.
sentences.zh: 他去了耶鲁法学院。

sentences.en: And during those studies, one of his professors was a gentleman named Samuel Huntington, the author of what was a very controversial book at the time
sentences.zh: 在学习期间，他的一位教授是一位名叫塞缪尔·亨廷顿的绅士，他是当时一本非常有争议的书的作者，

sentences.en: called The Clash of Civilizations that essentially argued that American culture was besieged primarily by Latino immigrants.
sentences.zh: 书名叫《文明的冲突》，该书本质上认为美国文化正受到拉丁裔移民的围攻。

sentences.en: And how did this politics of Chris Kobach that seemed very skeptical of immigration and anxious about what it could do to the United States, how did that evolve into the
sentences.zh: 那么克里斯·科巴赫这种似乎对移民非常怀疑、并对移民可能对美国造成的影响感到焦虑的政治观点，是如何演变成他现在所知的

sentences.en: issue of voter fraud for which he's now known?
sentences.zh: 选民欺诈问题的呢？

sentences.en: Well, I think when you're running for secretary of state in any state, voting is one of the central responsibilities of a secretary of state.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为当你竞选任何州的州务卿时，投票是州务卿的核心职责之一。

sentences.en: In most states, it's the secretary of state who is in charge of election oversight.
sentences.zh: 在大多数州，负责选举监督的正是州务卿。

sentences.en: And so it was to his political advantage, as it would be for any candidate for secretary of state, to make election security an issue.
sentences.zh: 因此，正如任何州务卿候选人一样，将选举安全作为一个议题对他来说在政治上是有利的。

sentences.en: Help me connect the dots here.
sentences.zh: 帮我理清一下思路。

sentences.en: How do views about immigration link with voter fraud?
sentences.zh: 关于移民的观点是如何与选民欺诈联系起来的？

sentences.en: Well, in Kansas, Mr. Kobach has made the argument that fraud, particularly by undocumented
sentences.zh: 嗯，在堪萨斯州，科巴赫先生提出了这样的论点：欺诈，特别是无证

sentences.en: immigrants or by foreigners who are not supposed to vote, maybe here illegally, but aren't supposed to vote, that this is one of the major causes of voter fraud in Kansas.
sentences.zh: 移民或不应该投票的外国人（也许是非法居留，但不应该投票），是堪萨斯州选民欺诈的主要原因之一。

sentences.en: And he has sort of knitted the idea of undocumented immigration, foreigners and voting into a single theory.
sentences.zh: 他把无证移民、外国人投票这些概念编织成了一个单一的理论。

sentences.en: And then what is the single theory that we've these elements together?
sentences.zh: 那么这个将这些要素结合在一起的单一理论是什么？

sentences.en: It's what Mr. Trump espoused, that we have potentially millions of undocumented people in this country who are nevertheless managing to vote and they're swaying the elections.
sentences.zh: 这就是特朗普先生所支持的观点，即我们国家有数百万潜在的无证人员，他们却设法投票并左右了选举。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So what has Chris Kobach done about this issue of voter fraud as secretary of state of Kansas?
sentences.zh: 那么作为堪萨斯州州务卿，克里斯·科巴赫在选民欺诈问题上做了什么？

sentences.en: He's been very active.
sentences.zh: 他非常积极。

sentences.en: He managed to persuade the state to pass a very unusual law.
sentences.zh: 他成功说服该州通过了一项非常不同寻常的法律。

sentences.en: It was called SAFE, which essentially required that anybody registering to vote in Kansas produce proof of citizenship, a birth certificate, a passport, naturalization papers.
sentences.zh: 它被称为 SAFE 法案，本质上要求任何在堪萨斯州登记投票的人必须提供公民身份证明，如出生证明、护照或入籍文件。

sentences.en: That law was passed in 2011.
sentences.zh: 该法律于2011年通过。

sentences.en: So before that law was passed, if you wanted to register to vote and then vote in Kansas, what was different?
sentences.zh: 那么在该法律通过之前，如果你想在堪萨斯州登记投票并投票，有什么不同？

sentences.en: Well, in Kansas, as in most every other state in the country, when you register to vote, you sign an affidavit.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在堪萨斯州，就像全国大多数其他州一样，当你登记投票时，你需要签署一份宣誓书。

sentences.en: Usually you tick off a box which says, I swear under penalty of perjury that I am a citizen in the United States.
sentences.zh: 通常你需要勾选一个方框，上面写着：我宣誓，如果作伪证将受惩罚，我是美国公民。

sentences.en: And if you're lying about that, you can be brought to trial and put in jail.
sentences.zh: 如果你在这方面撒谎，你可能会被起诉并入狱。

sentences.en: So most people think that that's a pretty strong deterrent against misrepresenting yourself.
sentences.zh: 所以大多数人认为这是一种相当强有力的威慑，防止人们虚报身份。

sentences.en: Thank you for calling the Concordia Audemarsk.
sentences.zh: 感谢您致电康考迪亚·奥德马斯克。

sentences.en: Please press one for the service center or press two for the sales department.
sentences.zh: 请按1转接服务中心，或按2转接销售部。

sentences.en: Concordia Audemarsk, this is Elaine.
sentences.zh: 康考迪亚·奥德马斯克，我是伊莱恩。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm trying.
sentences.zh: 你好，我正在尝试。

sentences.en: Oh, this is Elaine.
sentences.zh: 哦，我是伊莱恩。

sentences.en: Is this Senator Bowers?
sentences.zh: 请问是鲍尔斯参议员吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: I am fine.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: So I'm going to hop in the back room for private and I'll put you on hold and I'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我要去后屋处理点私事，把你转到等待线，我马上回来。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Just a sec.
sentences.zh: 稍等一下。

sentences.en: In addition to owning a car dealership, Elaine Bowers is also a Republican state senator in Kansas.
sentences.zh: 伊莱恩·鲍尔斯除了拥有一家汽车经销店外，还是堪萨斯州的一名共和党参议员。

sentences.en: She supports the SAFE Act and its voter ID requirements, but not because she thinks voter fraud is a significant problem in
sentences.zh: 她支持 SAFE 法案及其选民身份证要求，但并不是因为她认为选民欺诈在

sentences.en: Kansas.
sentences.zh: 堪萨斯州是一个严重的问题。

sentences.en: What convinced you that this was a bill worth voting for?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你相信这是一项值得投票支持的法案？

sentences.en: Well, there was no reason to vote against it, to tell you the truth.
sentences.zh: 老实说，没有理由投反对票。

sentences.en: It was common sense.
sentences.zh: 这是常识。

sentences.en: It's just something that we're used to carrying with us.
sentences.zh: 这只是我们习惯随身携带的东西。

sentences.en: And we have our wallets, our purses with us when we go to vote.
sentences.zh: 我们去投票时会带着钱包和手提包。

sentences.en: Anyhow, you don't buy a car without showing your ID.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，你不出示身份证就买不到车。

sentences.en: We can't get a library card without our ID.
sentences.zh: 没有身份证我们也办不到借书证。

sentences.en: We can't board a plane.
sentences.zh: 我们不能登机。

sentences.en: To me, that is proving who you are.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这就是证明你是谁。

sentences.en: You're a U.S.
sentences.zh: 你是美国

sentences.en: citizen.
sentences.zh: 公民。

sentences.en: And it's as simple as that.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这么简单。

sentences.en: It is our duty as a citizen, showing ID to prove who we are and where we come from.
sentences.zh: 作为公民，出示身份证证明我们是谁以及我们来自哪里，是我们的义务。

sentences.en: It works here in Kansas.
sentences.zh: 这在堪萨斯州行得通。

sentences.en: A lot of listeners don't get to hear from local lawmakers.
sentences.zh: 很多听众听不到当地立法者的声音。

sentences.en: And there are those who think that there's just not enough evidence of voter fraud to pass laws like this,
sentences.zh: 有些人认为没有足够的证据证明存在选民欺诈来通过这样的法律，

sentences.en: and that they see it as an attempt to keep certain people from voting, in particular, lower-income people, minorities.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这是一种阻止特定人群投票的企图，特别是低收入人群和少数族裔。

sentences.en: What do you say to those as somebody who has voted for one of these bills and who knows what it means to represent people in Kansas?
sentences.zh: 作为一名投票支持过此类法案、并且了解代表堪萨斯州人民意味着什么的人，你对这些人有什么想说的？

sentences.en: That was mentioned.
sentences.zh: 这一点被提到了。

sentences.en: I do recall that in the bill discussion.
sentences.zh: 我确实记得在法案讨论中提到过。

sentences.en: And as far as the worry about that, I think you have a duty as a U.S.
sentences.zh: 至于对此的担忧，我认为作为一名美国

sentences.en: citizen to vote.
sentences.zh: 公民，你有义务去投票。

sentences.en: It's the biggest duty, I believe.
sentences.zh: 我相信，这是最重要的职责。

sentences.en: And if voting is important to you, you will have an ID somehow.
sentences.zh: 如果投票对你来说很重要，你总会想办法弄到身份证件的。

sentences.en: Michael, what's been the effect of the SAFE Act in Kansas since it was passed by the legislature?
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，堪萨斯州的《安全法案》自立法机构通过以来，产生了什么影响？

sentences.en: Well, it's been under consistent legal assault ever since it was enacted.
sentences.zh: 嗯，自该法案颁布以来，它一直受到法律层面的持续抨击。

sentences.en: He was promptly sued.
sentences.zh: 他很快就遭到了起诉。

sentences.en: And in fact, he's been sued four times by the ACLU over aspects of this law.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他已经因为这项法律的某些条款被美国公民自由联盟（ACLU）起诉了四次。

sentences.en: So parts of it have been overturned or stayed.
sentences.zh: 所以其中的部分条款已经被推翻或中止执行了。

sentences.en: The other impact was that, in the word of one judge, thousands of people who had tried to register to vote in Kansas were not allowed to register because they didn't have the
sentences.zh: 另一个影响是，用一位法官的话说，成千上万试图在堪萨斯州登记投票的人，因为无法提供所需的证明文件，

sentences.en: documents that they needed.
sentences.zh: 而没能完成登记。

sentences.en: So folks who wanted to register legally found themselves turned away.
sentences.zh: 所以，那些想要合法登记的人发现自己被拒之门外了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What exactly is the argument against a law like the one in Kansas that Chris Kobach pushed for that asks people to provide just a basic piece of identification?
sentences.zh: 对于克里斯·科巴赫推动的堪萨斯州那种要求人们提供基本身份证明的法律，反对者的论点到底是什么？

sentences.en: Because the argument that you hear from supporters of the law is, we need ID to get on a plane.
sentences.zh: 因为你从该法案支持者那里听到的论点是：我们坐飞机需要身份证。

sentences.en: We need ID to get into a bar.
sentences.zh: 我们进酒吧需要身份证。

sentences.en: Why not have an ID for something as sacred as the ballot box?
sentences.zh: 为什么像投票箱这样神圣的事情，反而不需要身份证呢？

sentences.en: Well, the critics of this say that driving a car or going into a bar is not a constitutional right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，批评者认为，开车或去酒吧并不是宪法赋予的权利。

sentences.en: It's a privilege.
sentences.zh: 那是一种特权。

sentences.en: And there's a difference.
sentences.zh: 这两者是有区别的。

sentences.en: And you don't put restrictions on constitutional rights to the extent that you can avoid them.
sentences.zh: 而且，在能够避免的情况下，你不应该对宪法权利施加限制。

sentences.en: Some people are disproportionately affected.
sentences.zh: 有些人受到的影响是不成比例的。

sentences.en: And just to give you an example, in North Carolina, where a very extensive set of restrictions on voting
sentences.zh: 举个例子，在北卡罗来纳州，去年年底一套非常广泛的投票限制措施

sentences.en: was struck down late last year, the North Carolina law, which required people to produce a driver's
sentences.zh: 被推翻了。北卡罗来纳州的法律要求人们出示驾照

sentences.en: license and some other forms of identification, limited forms, was enacted after the state legislature
sentences.zh: 和其他一些有限的身份证明形式，该法律是在州立法机构

sentences.en: that was drafting the law requested racial data on who had a driver's license.
sentences.zh: 起草该法案时，索取了关于谁拥有驾照的种族数据后制定的。

sentences.en: And the racial data showed that African-Americans were disproportionately unlikely to have a driver's license.
sentences.zh: 而种族数据显示，非裔美国人拥有驾照的可能性不成比例地低。

sentences.en: And so that was made a requirement in order to vote.
sentences.zh: 所以这被设定为投票的必要条件。

sentences.en: So you're suggesting that in a place like that, there was a deliberate attempt to craft a law that
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，在那样的地方，有人蓄意制定了一项法律，

sentences.en: would make it harder for a specific group of people, in that case, African-Americans, to register to vote and vote.
sentences.zh: 旨在让特定群体——在这种情况下是非裔美国人——更难登记投票和参与投票。

sentences.en: I'm not saying it.
sentences.zh: 这不是我说的。

sentences.en: The Federal Court of Appeals said it.
sentences.zh: 是联邦上诉法院说的。

sentences.en: They said, in fact, that that law was crafted, as they put it, with almost surgical precision to discourage voting by African-Americans.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上说，这项法律的制定，用他们的话说，带有“近乎外科手术般的精确”，旨在阻碍非裔美国人投票。

sentences.en: The Republican legislature that drafted the law has denied that, but in any case says, look, we are not discriminating against black people.
sentences.zh: 起草该法律的共和党立法机构否认了这一点，但无论如何他们表示：看，我们并不是在歧视黑人。

sentences.en: We simply don't want Democrats to vote.
sentences.zh: 我们只是不想让民主党人投票。

sentences.en: Michael, has Chris Kobach been effective through this law and his various efforts in finding cases of voter fraud in Kansas?
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，克里斯·科巴赫通过这项法律以及他的各种努力，在堪萨斯州发现选民欺诈案件方面有效吗？

sentences.en: He has alleged to have turned up something like 125 instances of foreigners who were either registered to vote or had cast ballots.
sentences.zh: 他声称发现了大约125起外国人登记投票或参与投票的案例。

sentences.en: I think so far since 2011, he actually has prosecuted nine people.
sentences.zh: 我认为自2011年以来，他实际上只起诉了九个人。

sentences.en: I know that at least some of those people have made the argument that they were simply confused.
sentences.zh: 我知道其中至少有些人辩称他们只是搞混了。

sentences.en: So, Senator, what have voters in your district said about this issue of voting fraud, voter ID, and kind of the security of our voting system?
sentences.zh: 那么，参议员，你选区的选民对选民欺诈、选民身份证以及我们投票系统的安全性这些问题有什么看法？

sentences.en: Well, really, they believe there's other issues that are more important, like our taxes, our budget.
sentences.zh: 嗯，实际上，他们认为还有更重要的问题，比如我们的税收、我们的预算。

sentences.en: This is not something we talk about a lot.
sentences.zh: 这不是我们经常讨论的话题。

sentences.en: This is not national news to us back here.
sentences.zh: 这对我们这里的人来说不是什么全国性新闻。

sentences.en: And this is just a non-issue when we talk about this out in rural America.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论这些时，在乡村地区的美国，这根本不是个问题。

sentences.en: So I just want to make sure I understand something.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是想确保我理解了一些事情。

sentences.en: Kansas is now at the forefront, though, of voter ID laws and what many consider to be strict voter ID laws after that law in 2011.
sentences.zh: 不过，堪萨斯州现在确实处于选民身份证法的前沿，在2011年那项法律之后，它被许多人认为是严格的选民身份证法。

sentences.en: So how can we make sense of that discrepancy, which it kind of feels like it might be, that there's not so much
sentences.zh: 那么我们该如何理解这种差异呢？感觉好像在许多选区并没有那么多

sentences.en: anxiety about it in many districts, but Kansas is a leader in this kind of a change?
sentences.zh: 关于这方面的焦虑，但堪萨斯州却是这种变革的领导者？

sentences.en: Well, that would be our Secretary of State looking for voter fraud.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是因为我们的州务卿在寻找选民欺诈。

sentences.en: So our Secretary believes there is voter fraud, not only in Kansas, but across the nation.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的州务卿认为存在选民欺诈，不仅是在堪萨斯州，而是在全国范围内。

sentences.en: But that's something he is looking for, where as out in the real world of Kansas, this is not something that we think about that much.
sentences.zh: 但这正是他所寻找的东西，而在堪萨斯州的现实世界中，这并不是我们经常考虑的事情。

sentences.en: Michael, I want to talk about how what Chris Kobach did in Kansas connects back to the president's commission he's now leading.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，我想谈谈克里斯·科巴赫在堪萨斯州所做的事情，是如何与他现在领导的总统委员会联系起来的。

sentences.en: What's the commission done so far?
sentences.zh: 委员会目前做了什么？

sentences.en: Not a lot.
sentences.zh: 没做多少。

sentences.en: It hasn't had a formal meeting yet, although it did have a telephone session.
sentences.zh: 它还没有举行过正式会议，尽管进行过一次电话会议。

sentences.en: I think the first meeting is on July 19th.
sentences.zh: 我想第一次会议是在7月19日。

sentences.en: What it has done is to send out a letter to all 50 states requesting that they turn over their voter rolls and a cache of related data, including partial social security numbers,
sentences.zh: 它所做的是向所有50个州发出一封信，要求它们交出选民名单和相关数据缓存，包括部分社会安全号码、

sentences.en: felony records, and other personal or semi-personal information.
sentences.zh: 重罪记录以及其他个人或半个人信息。

sentences.en: They have essentially asked for the data on 200 million voters in this country to be turned over to the commission so that they can do analysis of it.
sentences.zh: 他们本质上要求将这个国家2亿选民的数据交给委员会，以便他们进行分析。

sentences.en: The commission has asked for social security numbers?
sentences.zh: 委员会要求提供社会安全号码？

sentences.en: It's asked for the last four digits of social security numbers.
sentences.zh: 它要求提供社会安全号码的后四位。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Well, because if you have, for instance, the last four digits of social security numbers, you can run a voter list against a social security database and find out who is where
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为如果你有社会安全号码的后四位，你就可以将选民名单与社会安全数据库进行比对，查出谁在哪里，

sentences.en: and whether they're qualified to vote.
sentences.zh: 以及他们是否有资格投票。

sentences.en: And to what end?
sentences.zh: 目的是什么？

sentences.en: What do they hope to find?
sentences.zh: 他们希望发现什么？

sentences.en: In general, it's a hunt for the fraud that they say exists.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，这是在搜寻他们所说的存在的欺诈行为。

sentences.en: And what have been the responses from the states?
sentences.zh: 各州的反应如何？

sentences.en: There has been a bipartisan resistance to this on the part of state election officials.
sentences.zh: 各州选举官员对此进行了两党一致的抵制。

sentences.en: Democrats have denounced it because Democrats argue that this panel is stacked from the very beginning.
sentences.zh: 民主党人谴责它，因为他们认为这个委员会从一开始就是被操纵的。

sentences.en: Many Democratic secretaries of state have simply said, we're not going to cooperate, period.
sentences.zh: 许多民主党籍的州务卿干脆说：我们不会配合，没门。

sentences.en: There has also been Republican opposition, and some of them simply have been upfront about rejecting it.
sentences.zh: 也有来自共和党的反对，其中一些人直接公开拒绝了它。

sentences.en: The secretary of state of Mississippi said that he would tell the commission members to go jump into the Gulf of Mexico.
sentences.zh: 密西西比州的州务卿说，他会告诉委员会成员去跳进墨西哥湾。

sentences.en: So presumably that secretary of state and others are not providing the requested information.
sentences.zh: 所以大概那位州务卿和其他人并没有提供所要求的信息。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What about Kansas?
sentences.zh: 堪萨斯州呢？

sentences.en: What is it doing?
sentences.zh: 它在做什么？

sentences.en: Well, it's sort of ironic.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这有点讽刺。

sentences.en: Kansas is providing all of the information except social security numbers, which, as Mr. Kobach has said, he can't provide because state law won't let him.
sentences.zh: 堪萨斯州提供了除社会安全号码之外的所有信息，正如科巴赫先生所说，他无法提供，因为州法律不允许他这样做。

sentences.en: So the secretary of state of Kansas, Chris Kobach, can't convince or allow his own state to fulfill the request he's asked of 50 states around the country.
sentences.zh: 所以堪萨斯州的州务卿克里斯·科巴赫，无法说服或允许他自己的州去满足他向全国50个州提出的要求。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's been an item of some confusion to those of us who watch this because, you know, Chris Kobach is a very smart man.
sentences.zh: 这对我们这些关注此事的人来说一直是个困惑，因为你知道，克里斯·科巴赫是一个非常聪明的人。

sentences.en: And as secretary of state, if he knows anything, he knows election law.
sentences.zh: 作为州务卿，如果他懂什么的话，那就是选举法。

sentences.en: And a lot of people don't have a clear idea why he would ask the states to provide information that clearly he knew they were unable to provide.
sentences.zh: 很多人不明白为什么他会要求各州提供他明明知道它们无法提供的信息。

sentences.en: What do you make of the fact that President Trump chose Chris Kobach to lead this commission on voter fraud?
sentences.zh: 你如何看待特朗普总统选择克里斯·科巴赫来领导这个选民欺诈委员会？

sentences.en: What does that tell us?
sentences.zh: 这告诉了我们什么？

sentences.en: President Trump appears to sincerely believe that he was cheated of the popular vote.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统似乎真诚地相信他在普选中被欺骗了。

sentences.en: And I think that he has appointed a commission that has people on it that also believe that voter fraud is a huge problem.
sentences.zh: 我认为他任命了一个委员会，里面的人也相信选民欺诈是一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: And critics of this commission say that it's basically stacked to produce a result that will favor the president, no matter what the evidence turns up.
sentences.zh: 而该委员会的批评者说，它基本上是被操纵的，旨在产生一个有利于总统的结果，无论证据显示什么。

sentences.en: So the SAFE Act, something like what happened in Kansas, could become national federal policy if the president and Chris Kobach and this commission get it there.
sentences.zh: 所以《安全法案》，类似于堪萨斯州发生的事情，如果总统、克里斯·科巴赫和这个委员会能做到的话，可能会成为全国性的联邦政策。

sentences.en: I think that, you know, the notion that voter fraud is persistent and undetected and needs to be reined in is right now a Republican article of faith, not just with Mr. Kobach.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道，认为选民欺诈是持续存在的、未被发现的并且需要加以遏制的观念，现在是共和党的一种信仰，不仅仅是科巴赫先生个人的想法。

sentences.en: And now that Republicans control Congress, I think there are many people who feel that they wouldn't be surprised at all if
sentences.zh: 现在共和党控制了国会，我认为有很多人觉得，如果委员会提出相关建议并引入一项法律，他们一点也不会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: the commission comes out with recommendations to that effect that a law would be introduced.
sentences.zh: 委员会提出相关建议并引入一项法律。

sentences.en: Michael Wines, thank you very much for this.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·温斯，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Last Friday was the deadline for state election officials to provide the personal records of their voters to Kobach's team.
sentences.zh: 上周五是各州选举官员向科巴赫团队提供选民个人记录的截止日期。

sentences.en: But after the intense backlash from those officials, and after three lawsuits were filed last week by civil rights groups, the commission has told states to hold off
sentences.zh: 但在这些官员的强烈抵制之后，以及民权组织上周提起三起诉讼之后，委员会已告知各州暂时

sentences.en: for now on sending the data.
sentences.zh: 搁置发送数据。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了吗？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间去突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他事情。

sentences.en: Senate Republicans say they are delaying this week's scheduled vote on the health care bill because Senator John McCain is recovering from surgery to
sentences.zh: 参议院共和党人表示，他们正在推迟本周原定的医疗法案投票，因为约翰·麦凯恩参议员正在从手术中恢复，

sentences.en: remove a blood clot above his left eye.
sentences.zh: 以切除他左眼上方的血块。

sentences.en: Without McCain, Republicans do not have the 50 votes they need, with Senators Susan Collins and Rand Paul already having said they will oppose the bill in its current form.
sentences.zh: 没有麦凯恩，共和党人就没有所需的50票，苏珊·柯林斯和兰德·保罗参议员已经表示他们将以目前的形式反对该法案。

sentences.en: The longer the bill's out there, the more conservative Republicans are going to discover that it's not repeal.
sentences.zh: 法案存在的时间越长，更多的保守派共和党人就会发现它根本不是废除。

sentences.en: Senator Paul, who has criticized the bill for leaving too much of the Affordable
sentences.zh: 保罗参议员曾批评该法案保留了太多的《平价医疗法案》内容，

sentences.en: Care Act in place, now predicts that the delay will give conservatives like him more time to organize against it.
sentences.zh: 他现在预测，推迟将给像他这样的保守派更多时间来组织反对它。

sentences.en: I think it's absolutely wrong.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是错误的。

sentences.en: It's not at all consistent with conservative principles, free market principles, or being a Republican.
sentences.zh: 这完全不符合保守派原则、自由市场原则，也不符合共和党的身份。

sentences.en: It also has nothing to do with repeal.
sentences.zh: 它也与废除毫无关系。

sentences.en: And we saw her change putters this week and it's working thus far.
sentences.zh: 我们看到她本周更换了推杆，到目前为止效果不错。

sentences.en: President Trump hosted the U.S.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统本周末在新泽西州的高尔夫俱乐部举办了美国女子公开赛。

sentences.en: Women's Open at his golf club in New Jersey this weekend.
sentences.zh: 女子公开赛。

sentences.en: Right in the middle.
sentences.zh: 就在中间。

sentences.en: That's a good putt there.
sentences.zh: 那一推不错。

sentences.en: Two under early.
sentences.zh: 早期低于标准杆两杆。

sentences.en: And sent out a flurry of tweets from there, defending his son Don Jr.
sentences.zh: 并从那里发出了一连串推文，为他的儿子小唐纳德辩护，

sentences.en: over his meeting with a Russian lawyer.
sentences.zh: 关于他与一名俄罗斯律师的会面。

sentences.en: In between those tweets, the president thanked people who had turned out to cheer for him at the tournament.
sentences.zh: 在这些推文之间，总统感谢了在锦标赛上为他欢呼的人们。

sentences.en: Thank you to all the supporters who far outnumbered the protesters yesterday at the
sentences.zh: 感谢昨天在女子美国公开赛上人数远超抗议者的支持者们，

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严格控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，该党就陷入了一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。
